:::{#def-cosine-sine}
#### Cosine

For a real number $\angpar$, start at the point $(1, 0)$ of the unit circle (@def-unit-circle)
and move a distance $\abs{\angpar}$ along the circle,
counterclockwise if $\angpar \ge 0$ and clockwise if $\angpar < 0$.
The first coordinate of the point reached is the **cosine** of $\angpar$, written $\cos\angpar$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-cosine-sine}
#### Cosines of some angles

- $\angpar = 0$ stays at $(1, 0)$, so $\cos 0 = 1$.
- $\angpar = \pi$ goes half way around the circle, to $(-1, 0)$, so $\cos\pi = -1$.
- $\angpar = \pi/2$ goes a quarter of the way round, to $(0, 1)$, so $\cos(\pi/2) = 0$.
- $\angpar = \pi/4$ goes an eighth of the way round,
  to the point of the circle with $x_1 = x_2 > 0$.
  There $x_1^2 + x_1^2 = 1$, so $x_1^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos(\pi/4) = x_1 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.7071$.

Angles are also measured in *degrees*, with a full turn of $2\pi$ equal to $360$ degrees,
so $\pi/2$ is $90$ degrees and $\pi/4$ is $45$ degrees.

:::
